# ciphertrust_proxy (Resource)

Configures outbound HTTP/HTTPS proxy settings (with optional CA certificate and no_proxy bypass list) for the CipherTrust Manager appliance. **Only available on CipherTrust Manager — not supported on CDSPaaS.**

This is a **singleton resource** — there is no Create or Delete operation at the CM API level. `terraform apply` always issues a PUT to configure proxy settings. `terraform destroy` removes the resource from Terraform state but does not clear the proxy configuration on CipherTrust Manager.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Terraform Configuration for CipherTrust Provider

# This configuration demonstrates the creation of an proxy resource
# with the CipherTrust provider, including setting up proxy details.

terraform {
  # Define the required providers for the configuration
  required_providers {
    # CipherTrust provider for managing CipherTrust resources
    ciphertrust = {
      # The source of the provider
      source = "ThalesGroup/CipherTrust"
      # Version of the provider to use
      version = "1.0.0-pre3"
    }
  }
}

# Configure the CipherTrust provider for authentication
provider "ciphertrust" {
	# The address of the CipherTrust appliance (replace with the actual address)
  address = "https://10.10.10.10"

  # Username for authenticating with the CipherTrust appliance
  username = "admin"

  # Password for authenticating with the CipherTrust appliance
  password = "ChangeMe101!"
}

# Add a resource of type proxy
resource "ciphertrust_proxy" "proxie" {
  http_proxy = "user01:test12345@10.171.18.190:8080"
  https_proxy = "user02:Test12345@10.171.18.190:8081"
  no_proxy = ["127.0.0.1", "localhost"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `certificate` (String) CA certificate to trust for proxy.
- `http_proxy` (String, Sensitive) HTTP proxy URL for proxy configurations. Sensitive. CipherTrust Manager masks passwords in GET responses; drift detection is limited when proxy credentials are used. If the proxy server's password contains any special character replace it with encoded values.
- `https_proxy` (String, Sensitive) HTTPS proxy URL for proxy configurations. Sensitive. CipherTrust Manager masks passwords in GET responses; drift detection is limited when proxy credentials are used. If the proxy server's password contains any special character replace it with encoded values.
- `no_proxy` (List of String) List of hosts for a proxy exception.

## Behavioral Notes

- **Singleton resource:** Only one proxy configuration exists per appliance. The provider uses `PUT /v1/configs/proxy` for both initial configuration and updates.
- **All attributes are mutable:** No attributes are immutable. Any attribute can be changed in-place without destroying and recreating the resource.
- **Clearing a proxy setting:** To remove a proxy URL, set the attribute to an empty string (`http_proxy = ""`). Omitting the attribute leaves the existing CM value unchanged.
- **Password masking:** CipherTrust Manager returns masked proxy URLs (e.g. `user:xxxxxx@host:port`) in GET responses. The provider preserves the Terraform state value when masking is detected to prevent spurious drift. Drift detection works fully for proxy URLs without credentials.
- **Drift detection:** Changes to proxy settings made outside Terraform surface as plan drift on the next `terraform plan`, unless the proxy URL contains a password (masked response).
- **Read() 404 behavior:** If the CM proxy endpoint returns 404, the provider emits a warning and removes the resource from Terraform state (`RemoveResource`). This is intentional for the singleton proxy: a 404 indicates a CM misconfiguration, not an OOB user deletion.
